source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: Chapter 9 exercise hal (PDF 208-211): MCQs jawab aur wajah ke saath, short, descriptive aur numerical sawalon ke model jawab, Kitab ki ghalti aur Wazahat boxes.

blocks.text: Yeh chapter 9 (Acid-Base Chemistry) ki exercise hai, kitab ki tarteeb mein, hal ke saath. Har MCQ ke saath sahi jawab aur wajah hai; short aur descriptive sawalon ke model jawab (poore number wale) aur numericals step by step hal kiye gaye hain. Kitab mein MCQs ki answer key nahi chhapi; jawab chapter ke text se nikale gaye hain.

blocks.prompt:
I. Given the following reaction:
NH₃(g) + H₂O(l) → NH₄⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq)
(Is reaction mein acid aur base kaun hain?)

options.text: NH₃ acid hai, H₂O base hai
NH₃ base hai, H₂O acid hai
NH₄⁺ base hai, OH⁻ acid hai
H₂O base hai, OH⁻ acid hai

blocks.explanation: H₂O proton (H⁺) deta hai, is liye acid hai; NH₃ proton leta hai, is liye base hai. NH₄⁺ NH₃ ka conjugate acid aur OH⁻ H₂O ka conjugate base hai (9.1).

blocks.prompt:
II. The pH of 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³ of an aqueous solution of H₂SO₄ is:
(10⁻³ mol dm⁻³ H₂SO₄ ke aqueous solution ki pH kya hai?)
blocks.explanation:
H₂SO₄ strong dibasic acid hai: har molecule 2H⁺ deta hai.
[H⁺] = 2 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³
pH = −log(2 × 10⁻³) = 3 − 0.30 = 2.7

blocks.prompt:
III. The solubility product of AgCl is 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ mol dm⁻⁶. The maximum concentration of Ag⁺ ions in the solution is:
(AgCl ka solubility product 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ hai. Solution mein Ag⁺ ions ka zyada se zyada concentration kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation:
AgCl(s) ⇌ Ag⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq); saturated solution mein [Ag⁺] = [Cl⁻] = S
Ksp = S² = 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁰
S = √(2.0 × 10⁻¹⁰) = 1.41 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: AgCl ke Ksp ka unit 'mol dm⁻⁶' chhapa hai. Ksp = [Ag⁺][Cl⁻] hai, is liye sahi unit mol² dm⁻⁶ hai.

blocks.prompt:
IV. Which indicator is typically used for titrations involving strong acids and strong bases?
(Strong acid aur strong base ki titration mein aam tor par kaun sa indicator istemal hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: Strong acid-strong base titration mein end point par pH taqreeban 4.0 se 10.0 tak achanak barhti hai, is liye phenolphthalein (range 8.2-10.0) istemal hota hai (9.9.2). Litmus ka rang wazeh (sharp) nahi badalta, is liye titration mein nahi lete.

blocks.prompt:
V. Which of the following is the conjugate base of water?
(Pani (water) ka conjugate base kaun sa hai?)
blocks.explanation: Pani proton de kar OH⁻ banta hai: H₂O → OH⁻ + H⁺. Is liye OH⁻ pani ka conjugate base hai; H₃O⁺ pani ka conjugate acid hai (9.1).

blocks.prompt:
Which of the following is a Lewis acid but not a Bronsted-Lowry acid?
(Kaun sa Lewis acid hai lekin Bronsted-Lowry acid nahi?)
blocks.explanation: AlCl₃ ke paas dene ke liye proton nahi, lekin is ke Al ka octet adhoora (incomplete) hai (BF₃ ke B ki tarah), is liye yeh electron pair leta hai: sirf Lewis acid. HCl aur H₂O proton dete hain; NH₃ base hai (9.2).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Item V mein do sawal aik number ke neeche chhape hain: pehle sawal (pani ka conjugate base) ke options aik line mein hain aur OH⁻(aq) se pehle 'a.' nahi chhapa; doosre sawal (Lewis acid) ka apna number nahi. Dono yahan hal kiye gaye hain.

blocks.prompt:
VI. In an acid-base titration, the equivalence point is reached when:
(Acid-base titration mein equivalence point kab aata hai?)

options.text: Jab acid aur base ke barabar volumes daal diye jayein

blocks.explanation: Equivalence point tab aata hai jab daale gaye base ki miqdar (moles) acid ki miqdar ke stoichiometrically barabar ho jaye (9.9.2). (a) sirf strong acid-strong base mein sahi hai; (b) end point hai, equivalence point nahi.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Koi option bilkul durust nahi. Equivalence point par acid aur base ke moles stoichiometrically barabar (equivalent) hote hain (9.9.2); barabar volume sirf tab chahiye jab dono solutions ka concentration barabar ho (1:1 reaction mein). (a) pH 7.0 sirf strong acid-strong base titration mein hota hai, (b) rang ka badalna end point hai jo sirf equivalence point ke qareeb hota hai, aur (d) reaction yun hi 'ruk' nahi jata. Murad jawab (c) hai: 'equal volumes' ko 'barabar moles' parhein.

blocks.prompt:
VII. If the concentration of Cl⁻ ion in a solution is increased, the solubility of silver chloride (AgCl) will:
(Solution mein Cl⁻ ka concentration barhane se AgCl ki solubility (hal pazeeri) par kya asar hoga?)
blocks.explanation: Cl⁻ common ion hai: [Ag⁺][Cl⁻] Ksp se barh jata hai, equilibrium AgCl(s) ⇌ Ag⁺ + Cl⁻ baayein taraf jata hai aur AgCl neeche baith jata hai (common ion effect, 9.6). Solubility kam hoti hai, zero nahi hoti.

blocks.prompt:
VIII. Which of the following pairs of substances can act as a conjugate acid-base pair according to the Bronsted-Lowry theory?
(Bronsted-Lowry theory ke mutabiq kaun sa jora conjugate acid-base pair hai?)
blocks.explanation: Conjugate pair mein sirf aik proton ka farq hota hai: NH₄⁺ − H⁺ = NH₃ (9.1).

blocks.prompt:
IX. If the pH of a solution is 11, what is the [OH⁻] concentration in the solution?
(Agar solution ki pH 11 ho to [OH⁻] kitna hai?)

X. Which of the following pairs forms a buffer solution?
(Kaun sa jora buffer solution banata hai?)
blocks.explanation: Acidic buffer weak acid aur us ke strong base wale namak (salt) se banta hai: CH₃COOH + CH₃COONa (9.7). HCl strong acid hai, NaOH + HCl sirf neutralize hote hain, aur Na₂SO₄ NH₃ ka salt nahi.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Option (d) mein band karne wali bracket nahi chhapi: 'sodium sulfate (Na₂SO₄'. Sahi: sodium sulfate (Na₂SO₄).

blocks.prompt:
XI. What is the purpose of a titration acid-base curve?
(Acid-base titration curve ka maqsad kya hai?)

options.text: Istemal hone wale acid ya base ka volume naapna
Titration ke mukhtalif marahil par pH maloom karna

blocks.explanation: pH curve daale gaye titrant ke volume ke muqable mein pH ka graph hai; yeh dikhata hai ke titration ke dauran pH kaise badalti hai aur indicator chunne mein madad karta hai (9.9.2).

blocks.prompt:
a. Define the following with an example for each:
i) Ionization constant
ii) Solubility product
ii) Common ion effect
iv) Acid-base Indicator
In ki tareef (definition) misal ke saath likhein.
blocks.explanation:
i) Ionization constant (Ka): weak acid ke ionization (ions mein tootne) ka equilibrium constant, Ka = [H₃O⁺][A⁻]/[HA]; misal: CH₃COOH, Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵.
ii) Solubility product (Ksp): kam hal hone wale (sparingly soluble) salt ke saturated solution mein ions ke molar concentrations ka hasil-e-zarb, har aik apne coefficient ki power ke saath; misal: PbSO₄, Ksp = [Pb²⁺][SO₄²⁻] = 1.6 × 10⁻⁸ (25 °C).
iii) Common ion effect: weak electrolyte mein usi ion wala strong electrolyte daalne se us ka ionization dab (suppress) jana; misal: NH₄Cl daalne se NH₃ (NH₄OH) ka ionization kam ho jata hai.
iv) Acid-base indicator: weak organic acid ya base jo rang badal kar end point batata hai; misal: phenolphthalein, acid mein be-rang aur base mein gulabi-surkh (pH 8.2-10.0).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Teesri term par dobara 'ii)' chhapa hai; sahi number iii) Common ion effect hai.

blocks.prompt:
b. Differentiate between:
i) Hydrolysis and dissolution
Hydrolysis aur dissolution mein farq likhein.
blocks.explanation: Dissolution mein salt sirf pani mein ions mein toot-ta hai; hydrolysis mein yeh ions pani se reaction bhi karte hain aur pH badal dete hain.

rows: Salt ke ions pani se reaction karte hain
Salt sirf hal ho kar ions mein alag hota hai
H₃O⁺ ya OH⁻ bante hain, pH badalti hai
H₃O⁺ ya OH⁻ nahi bante, pH wohi rehti hai
Weak acid ya weak base ke salts, misal NH₄⁺ + H₂O ⇌ NH₃ + H₃O⁺
Misal NaCl(s) → Na⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq); solution neutral rehta hai

blocks.prompt:
b. ii) Acidic and basic buffer solutions
Acidic aur basic buffer solutions mein farq likhein.
blocks.explanation: Dono pH ki tabdeeli ko rokte hain; farq un ke ajza (components) aur pH mein hai.

rows: Weak acid + us ka strong base wala salt
Weak base + us ka strong acid wala salt
pH 7 se kam
pH 7 se zyada
Misal CH₃COOH + CH₃COONa (barabar concentration par pH 4.74)
Misal NH₄OH + NH₄Cl

blocks.prompt:
c. Explain the concept of conjugate acid-base pairs. How are they related in terms of proton transfer?
Conjugate acid-base pairs ka tasawwur samjhayein. Proton transfer ke lehaz se in ka kya taluq hai?
blocks.explanation:
Jo acid proton deta hai woh apna conjugate base ban jata hai; jo base proton leta hai woh apna conjugate acid ban jata hai. Jore ke dono hisson mein sirf aik proton (H⁺) ka farq hota hai.
HCl + H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻: jore HCl/Cl⁻ aur H₃O⁺/H₂O.

blocks.prompt:
d. What is the relationship between the strength of an acid and the strength of its conjugate base?
Acid ki taqat aur us ke conjugate base ki taqat mein kya taluq hai?
blocks.explanation:
Ulta (inverse) taluq hai: acid jitna strong, us ka conjugate base utna weak.
HCl strong acid hai is liye Cl⁻ bohat weak base hai (pH par asar nahi); CH₃COOH weak acid hai is liye CH₃COO⁻ nisbatan strong base hai aur hydrolysis se OH⁻ deta hai.

blocks.prompt:
e. For the following three reactions, identify the reactants that are Arrhenius bases, Bronsted-Lowry bases, and/or Lewis bases. State which type(s) of bases each reactant is. Explain your answers.
i) NaOH(s) → Na⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq)
i) HF(aq) + H₂O(l) → F⁻(aq) + H₃O⁺(aq)
ii) H⁺(aq) + NH₃(aq) → NH₄⁺(aq)
Teeno reactions mein Arrhenius, Bronsted-Lowry aur/ya Lewis base pehchanein aur wajah batayein.
blocks.explanation:
Reaction 1: NaOH Arrhenius base hai, kyunke pani mein OH⁻ ions deta hai.
Reaction 2: H₂O Bronsted-Lowry base hai (HF se proton leta hai) aur Lewis base bhi (is ka O atom H⁺ ko lone pair deta hai).
Reaction 3: NH₃ Bronsted-Lowry base hai (H⁺ leta hai) aur Lewis base bhi (N ka lone pair H⁺ ke saath coordinate bond banata hai).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Teen reactions par number i), i), ii) chhape hain; sahi numbering i), ii), iii) hai.

blocks.prompt:
f. An amphoteric substance can behave as either an acid or a base. Identify whether water behaves as an acid or a base in each of the following reactions.
i) H₂O + HCl → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻
ii) NH₃ + H₂O → NH₄⁺ + OH⁻
iii) HNO₃ + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + NO₃⁻
iv) CH₃COOH + H₂O ↔ CH₃COO⁻ + H₃O⁺
Amphoteric cheez acid ya base dono ban sakti hai. Har reaction mein batayein ke pani acid hai ya base.
blocks.explanation:
i) Base: pani HCl se H⁺ le kar H₃O⁺ banta hai.
ii) Acid: pani NH₃ ko H⁺ de kar OH⁻ banta hai.
iii) Base: pani HNO₃ se H⁺ leta hai.
iv) Base: pani CH₃COOH se H⁺ leta hai (reversible reaction, ⇌).

blocks.prompt:
g. Which salt would you expect to dissolve more readily in acidic solution: Barium sulfate or Barium fluoride? Explain.
Acidic solution mein kaun sa salt zyada asaani se hal hoga: barium sulfate ya barium fluoride? Wajah batayein.
blocks.explanation:
Barium fluoride. F⁻ weak acid HF ka conjugate base hai, is liye H⁺ ise khatam karta hai: H⁺ + F⁻ → HF. [F⁻] kam hota hai, ionic product Ksp se neeche aata hai aur zyada BaF₂ hal hota hai (BaF₂(s) ⇌ Ba²⁺ + 2F⁻ daayein taraf).
SO₄²⁻ strong acid H₂SO₄ se hai aur bohat weak base hai, is liye acid ise nahi hatata aur BaSO₄ hal nahi hota.

blocks.prompt:
h. Why does common ion effect decrease solubility of a less soluble salt?
Common ion effect kam hal hone wale salt ki solubility kyun kam karta hai?
blocks.explanation:
Common ion daalne se ionic product Ksp se barh jata hai. Ksp ko qaim rakhne ke liye equilibrium baayein taraf jata hai aur salt neeche baith jata hai (precipitate), is liye kam salt hal rehta hai.
Misal: saturated AgCl mein NaCl: AgCl(s) ⇌ Ag⁺ + Cl⁻ baayein taraf.

blocks.prompt:
i. State the basic principle of solubility product. Mention factors affecting solubility product.
Solubility product ka bunyadi usool bayan karein. Is par asar daalne wale factors likhein.
blocks.explanation:
Usool: kisi khaas temperature par kam hal hone wale salt ke saturated solution mein ions ke concentrations ka hasil-e-zarb (har aik apne coefficient ki power ke saath) constant rehta hai, misal Ksp = [Pb²⁺][SO₄²⁻].
Factors: Ksp temperature aur salt (aur solvent) ki nature par munhasir hai. Common ion salt ki solubility kam karta hai, Ksp nahi badalta.

blocks.prompt:
j. What is the main reason that titration of weak acids with weak bases are not performed for volumetric analysis?
Weak acid ki weak base se titration volumetric analysis mein kyun nahi ki jati?
blocks.explanation: Weak acid-weak base titration mein equivalence point ke qareeb pH aahista aahista badalti hai; achanak jump nahi hota. Is liye koi indicator wazeh (sharp) rang nahi badalta aur end point theek maloom nahi hota.

blocks.prompt:
k. Prove by equations what happens when Na₂CrO₄ is added to saturated solution of PbCrO₄.
Equations se sabit karein ke PbCrO₄ ke saturated solution mein Na₂CrO₄ daalne se kya hota hai.
blocks.explanation:
PbCrO₄(s) ⇌ Pb²⁺(aq) + CrO₄²⁻(aq)
Na₂CrO₄(aq) → 2Na⁺(aq) + CrO₄²⁻(aq)
CrO₄²⁻ common ion hai; [Pb²⁺][CrO₄²⁻] Ksp se barh jata hai, is liye Pb²⁺(aq) + CrO₄²⁻(aq) → PbCrO₄(s). Equilibrium baayein taraf jata hai, PbCrO₄ neeche baithta hai aur us ki solubility kam hoti hai (common ion effect).

blocks.prompt:
l. According to the Lewis acid-base concept, Boron trifluoride (BF₃) can act as an acid. Is this statement correct?
Lewis concept ke mutabiq BF₃ acid ka kaam kar sakta hai. Kya yeh baat durust hai?
blocks.explanation:
Haan. BF₃ ke B ke paas sirf chhe valence electrons hain (adhoora octet), is liye yeh Lewis base se electron pair le kar coordinate bond banata hai:
BF₃ + F⁻ → BF₄⁻ (aur BF₃ + NH₃ → F₃B←NH₃).

blocks.prompt:
m. If the concentration of hydrogen ions in a solution is 1 × 10⁻⁵ M, what is the pH of the solution?
Agar solution mein hydrogen ions ka concentration 1 × 10⁻⁵ M ho to pH kya hogi?
blocks.explanation:
Diya gaya: [H⁺] = 1 × 10⁻⁵ M
Formula: pH = −log[H⁺]
pH = −log(1 × 10⁻⁵)
pH = 5
Solution acidic hai (pH < 7).

blocks.prompt:
Q.3 Describe the Bronsted-Lowry theory of acids and bases. Provide examples of conjugate acid-base pairs and explain clearly their relationship.
Bronsted-Lowry theory bayan karein. Conjugate acid-base pairs ki misalein dein aur un ka taluq wazeh karein.
blocks.explanation:
Theory (1923, Bronsted aur Lowry): acid woh hai jo proton (H⁺) de (proton donor) aur base woh hai jo proton le (proton acceptor). Yeh pani ke baghair bhi kaam karti hai, jo Arrhenius theory nahi samjha sakti.
Misalein:
1. HCl(g) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₃O⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq): HCl acid, H₂O base; jore HCl/Cl⁻ aur H₃O⁺/H₂O.
2. NH₃(g) + H₂O(l) ⇌ NH₄⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq): H₂O acid, NH₃ base; jore NH₄⁺/NH₃ aur H₂O/OH⁻.
3. HCl(g) + NH₃(g) → NH₄Cl(s): solvent aur OH⁻ ke baghair proton transfer.
Doosre jore (Table 9.1): HNO₃/NO₃⁻, H₂SO₄/HSO₄⁻, HCO₃⁻/CO₃²⁻.
Taluq: (i) jore ke dono hisson mein aik proton ka farq; (ii) acid − H⁺ = conjugate base, base + H⁺ = conjugate acid; (iii) acid jitna strong, conjugate base utna weak; (iv) pani amphoteric hai: HCl ke saath base, NH₃ ke saath acid.

blocks.prompt:
Q.4 Define the Lewis theory of acids and bases. How does this theory differ from the Bronsted-Lowry theory? Give examples of Lewis acids and bases that do not involve proton transfer.
Lewis theory ki tareef karein. Yeh Bronsted-Lowry theory se kaise mukhtalif hai? Aisi Lewis acids aur bases ki misalein dein jin mein proton transfer nahi hota.
blocks.explanation:
Lewis theory (1923, G.N. Lewis): Lewis acid woh hai jo electron pair le (accept kare) aur Lewis base woh hai jo electron pair de (donate kare); dono coordinate covalent bond bana kar adduct banate hain.
Proton transfer ke baghair misalein:
1. BF₃ + F⁻ → BF₄⁻ (BF₃ acid, adhoora octet; F⁻ base).
2. Ag⁺ + 2NH₃ → [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ (Ag⁺ acid; har NH₃ apna lone pair deta hai).
3. BF₃ + NH₃ → F₃B←NH₃; SO₃ + O²⁻ → SO₄²⁻; AlCl₃ bhi Lewis acid hai.

rows: Proton (H⁺) ke transfer par mabni
Electron pair par mabni
Acid = proton dene wala, base = proton lene wala
Acid = electron pair lene wala, base = electron pair dene wala
Acid mein hydrogen hona zaroori
Acid mein hydrogen zaroori nahi (BF₃, AlCl₃, Ag⁺)
BF₃ ya Ag⁺ ko acid nahi samjha sakti
Zyada wasee: har Bronsted base Lewis base bhi hai

blocks.prompt:
Q.5 Discuss applications and implications of the common ion effect in various fields.
Mukhtalif shobon mein common ion effect ke istemal (applications) aur asraat bayan karein.
blocks.explanation:
Common ion effect: usi ion wala strong electrolyte daalne se weak ya kam hal hone wale electrolyte ka ionization (ya solubility) dab jata hai.
Istemal:
1. Namak (NaCl) ki safai: brine mein HCl gas guzarne se [Cl⁻] barhta hai aur khalis NaCl crystals ban kar nikal aata hai.
2. Kam hal salt ko neeche bithana: KClO₃ solution mein KCl (common K⁺) daalne se KClO₃ neeche baith jata hai.
3. Salt analysis group II: HCl (common H⁺) H₂S ⇌ 2H⁺ + S²⁻ ko dabata hai, kam [S²⁻] se sirf group II ke sulfides girte hain.
4. Salt analysis group III: NH₄Cl (common NH₄⁺) NH₄OH ko dabata hai, kam [OH⁻] se sirf group III ke hydroxides girte hain.
5. Buffers: CH₃COONa CH₃COOH ke ionization ko dabata hai (aur NH₄Cl NH₄OH ko), is se taqreeban muqarrar pH wale solutions bante hain; khoon ka bicarbonate buffer khoon ki pH qaim rakhta hai.
Asraat: common ion kam hal salt ki solubility hamesha kam karta hai (NaCl mein AgCl, Na₂CrO₄ mein PbCrO₄) aur acid-base equilibria ko badal kar pH aur precipitation ko control karta hai.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Common ion effect Le Chatelier ke usool ki aik soorat hai: equilibrium ki kisi aik cheez (ion) ko barhao to equilibrium ulti taraf ja kar us ion ko kam karne ki koshish karta hai.

blocks.prompt:
Q.6 What is the solubility product for sparingly soluble salts. Give its two applications.
Kam hal hone wale salts ke liye solubility product kya hai? Is ke do istemal likhein.
blocks.explanation:
Solubility product (Ksp): kam hal salt apne saturated solution ke saath equilibrium mein ho, misal PbSO₄(s) ⇌ Pb²⁺(aq) + SO₄²⁻(aq), to solid ka concentration constant rehta hai, is liye Kc[PbSO₄] = Ksp = [Pb²⁺][SO₄²⁻] = 1.6 × 10⁻⁸ (25 °C). Yeh ions ke concentrations ka hasil-e-zarb hai, har aik balanced equation ke coefficient ki power ke saath (PbCl₂: Ksp = [Pb²⁺][Cl⁻]²). Yeh chhota hota hai aur temperature par munhasir hai.
Istemal 1, Ksp se solubility: Ca(OH)₂ ⇌ Ca²⁺ + 2OH⁻; Ksp = S(2S)² = 4S³ = 6.5 × 10⁻⁶, to S = 1.18 × 10⁻² mol dm⁻³, [Ca²⁺] = 1.18 × 10⁻² aur [OH⁻] = 2.36 × 10⁻² mol dm⁻³.
Istemal 2, precipitation ki peshgoi: 10⁻² mol dm⁻³ Ca²⁺ aur SO₄²⁻ ke barabar volume milane se har aik 5.0 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³; ionic product = 2.5 × 10⁻⁵ > CaSO₄ ka Ksp (2 × 10⁻⁵), is liye CaSO₄ girta hai. Ionic product > Ksp: precipitate; = Ksp: saturated; < Ksp: precipitate nahi.
(Common ion effect bhi: Na₂CrO₄ se PbCrO₄ girta hai.)

blocks.prompt:
Q.7 Describe the general shape of a titration curve for a strong acid titrated with a strong base. How can you identify the equivalence point on a titration curve for a strong acid-strong base titration?
Strong acid ki strong base se titration ke curve ki aam shakal bayan karein. Is curve par equivalence point kaise pehchante hain?
blocks.explanation:
Shakal (HCl ki NaOH se titration; daale gaye NaOH ke volume ke muqable mein pH):
1. Shuru: sirf strong acid, poora ionize; [H⁺] zyada, pH bohat kam.
2. Equivalence se pehle: OH⁻ H⁺ ko neutralize karta hai; pH aahista barhti hai, curve taqreeban seedha (flat).
3. Equivalence ke qareeb: bohat thore base se pH taqreeban 4.0 se 10.0 tak achanak (seedhi khari lakeer ki tarah) barhti hai.
4. Equivalence ke baad: OH⁻ zyada; curve oonchi pH par phir flat ho jata hai.
Equivalence point: daale gaye OH⁻ ke moles shuru ke H⁺ ke moles ke barabar. Curve par yeh seedhe khare hisse ka darmiyan hai, strong acid-strong base mein pH 7.0. Is hisse mein rang badalne wala indicator (phenolphthalein 8.2-10.0, ya methyl orange) ise end point ke tor par dikhata hai.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Curve ko yun yaad rakhein: shuru mein neeche flat, beech mein seedhi oonchi chhalang (steep jump), aakhir mein oopar flat. Chhalang ka beech = equivalence point.

blocks.prompt:
Q.8 A buffer solution has a pH of 5.0. It is made from a weak acid HA with a pKa of 4.8. What is the ratio of the concentration of the conjugate base [A⁻] to the concentration of the weak acid [HA] in this buffer?
Buffer ki pH 5.0 hai aur weak acid HA ka pKa 4.8 hai. [A⁻]/[HA] ki nisbat (ratio) kya hai?
blocks.explanation:
Diya gaya: pH = 5.0, pKa = 4.8
Maloom karna: [A⁻]/[HA]
Henderson equation: pH = pKa + log([A⁻]/[HA])
5.0 = 4.8 + log([A⁻]/[HA])
log([A⁻]/[HA]) = 5.0 − 4.8 = 0.2
[A⁻]/[HA] = antilog 0.2 = 10⁰·² = 1.58
Nisbat [A⁻] : [HA] ≈ 1.6 : 1

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: pH pKa se zyada hai, is liye buffer mein conjugate base (salt) acid se zyada hona chahiye: ratio 1 se bara (1.6) aaya, jo theek hai.

blocks.prompt:
Q.9 Calculate the solubility of a sparingly salt lead (II) iodide (PbI₂) in water. It has Ksp = 1.4 × 10⁻⁸.
Pani mein PbI₂ ki solubility hisaab karein. Ksp = 1.4 × 10⁻⁸.
blocks.explanation:
Diya gaya: PbI₂ ka Ksp = 1.4 × 10⁻⁸
Maloom karna: molar solubility S
PbI₂(s) ⇌ Pb²⁺(aq) + 2I⁻(aq)
Equilibrium par: [Pb²⁺] = S, [I⁻] = 2S
Ksp = [Pb²⁺][I⁻]² = S × (2S)² = 4S³
4S³ = 1.4 × 10⁻⁸
S³ = 1.4 × 10⁻⁸ / 4 = 3.5 × 10⁻⁹
S = ∛(3.5 × 10⁻⁹) = 1.52 × 10⁻³
S = 1.5 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Sawal mein 'a sparingly salt' chhapa hai; sahi 'a sparingly soluble salt' (kam hal hone wala salt) hai.

blocks.prompt:
Q.10 The molar solubility of silver chromate (Ag₂CrO₄) in pure water at 298 K is 6.5 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³. Calculate the Ksp of silver chromate at this temperature.
298 K par khalis pani mein Ag₂CrO₄ ki molar solubility 6.5 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³ hai. Is ka Ksp hisaab karein.
blocks.explanation:
Diya gaya: S = 6.5 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³, T = 298 K
Maloom karna: Ksp
Ag₂CrO₄(s) ⇌ 2Ag⁺(aq) + CrO₄²⁻(aq)
[Ag⁺] = 2S = 1.3 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³, [CrO₄²⁻] = S = 6.5 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³
Ksp = [Ag⁺]²[CrO₄²⁻] = (2S)² × S = 4S³
Ksp = 4 × (6.5 × 10⁻⁵)³
Ksp = 4 × 2.746 × 10⁻¹³
Ksp = 1.1 × 10⁻¹² mol³ dm⁻⁹

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Ag₂CrO₄ se do Ag⁺ bante hain, is liye [Ag⁺] = 2S hai aur Ksp mein yeh square hota hai: (2S)² = 4S². Yahi wajah hai ke jawab 4S³ aata hai, S³ nahi.
